observations: Photo shows a window/portable-style air conditioner unit (single body) with front grille and top air outlet.
Brand/model text appears on the front label area, but it is not clearly readable in this photo.
Unit looks dusty/used; no obvious broken parts visible from this angle.
Seller says it is faulty, but the photo does not show the fault (no screen/error code, no running test).

claims.claim: Faulty inverter AC available for sale.
claims.evidence: Photo 0 shows an AC unit but provides no proof of inverter type or the specific fault.

risks.risk: Whether it is actually inverter (vs non-inverter) and the exact capacity (e.g., 1HP/1.5HP/2HP) which strongly affects value.
risks.proof: A clear close-up photo of the rating plate/label showing brand, model, and capacity (HP/BTU) and whether it states inverter.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as a generic faulty AC with unknown capacity (worst-case value for repair/parts).

risks.risk: Fault type: compressor failure, gas leak, fan/motor issue, PCB/control issue—each has very different repair costs.
risks.proof: Video of power-on showing any error code/LED behavior plus a short running test (even if it fails) and sound check (compressor/fan start).
risks.if_unproven: Priced as not working / major fault (worst-case).

risks.risk: Missing parts or damaged fins/coil from transport or prior repair.
risks.proof: Photos of both sides and the back/coil area (including any exposed copper lines) and a close-up of the fins for bends.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as needing inspection and possible parts replacement.

risks.risk: Refrigerant status (gas leak) which may make it uneconomical to repair.
risks.proof: Technician test result: manifold gauge reading or leak test report (photo/screenshot).
risks.if_unproven: Priced as if refrigerant may be low/leaking (worst-case repair).

proof_requests: Clear close-up of the rating plate/label (brand, model, capacity/HP or BTU, and inverter wording).
Video of the unit being powered on: show any error lights/codes and whether compressor and fan start.
Photos of the back/side where the condenser coil and copper pipes are visible (and any damage).
If possible: technician’s diagnosis (compressor/gas/PCB/fan) or a short test report.
response.reason: The photo shows an AC unit, but the key details needed to price it correctly (exact model/capacity/inverter confirmation and the fault type) are not verifiable from the single image.
